suggested_experiment.question: Is the invagination driven by spontaneous curvature (wedge) or cortical force (actin)?
suggested_experiment.observable: cortical actin-density channel co-imaged with the membrane
suggested_experiment.intervention: acute actin depolymerization (e.g. latrunculin) OR amphipathic-helix (H0) mutation
suggested_experiment.predicted_contrast: actin_only / wedge+actin: invagination stalls or reverses when actin is depolymerized; wedge_only: invagination proceeds. H0 mutation removes curvature drive in the wedge models only.
suggested_experiment.rationale: c_eff_max and active_force_max are degenerate from geometry(t) alone (they trade off in the cap energy). An independent actin readout or a targeted perturbation breaks the degeneracy, which the recovery validation shows lifts active_force to identified.

method: Each hypothesis is a restricted forward model (subset of free forces; others at null). Ranked by nested-sampling log-evidence logZ (built-in Occam penalty). Decisive if top model's ln Bayes factor over runner-up >= 2.5. The actin-density likelihood term applies to ALL hypotheses (wedge-only predicts zero actin, penalized against real signal) so evidence is compared on identical data. When UNDETERMINED, a disambiguating experiment is proposed.
headline: The SAME movie is decisively wedge+actin WITH the actin channel (lnB=19.9) but UNDETERMINED from geometry alone (lnB=0.25) -> engine proposes actin imaging / latrunculin / H0-mutation.
